# Job #33: STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC
## Power-Stage Loss Model, Thermal Analysis, Bi-Directional DShot600 DMA Allocation, and Reference Netlist

---

## 0. Scope and Constraints

**System partitioning.** The STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and generates DShot600. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by the ESC MCU (e.g., AT32F421 or STM32G071 running AM32/BLHeli_32), not by the H743. ArduPilot never sees the 48 kHz carrier, so the two domains are modeled separately.

**Feasibility warning.** A "nano" footprint (20×20 or 25.5×25.5 mm mounting) cannot physically host 24 MOSFETs capable of 80 A continuous. Section 3 shows that 80 A per channel is a **transient, thermal-capacitance-limited rating of a few seconds**, not a steady-state capability.

**Assumptions.** All device parameters below are representative values and must be replaced with your chosen parts' datasheet values. Every equation is parametric so the numbers can be re-run.

| Symbol | Meaning | Baseline value |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | 6S full charge (worst case for switching) | 25.2 V |
| I_pk | Burst phase current per channel | 80 A |
| f_sw | ESC PWM frequency | 48 kHz |
| R_ds,25 | MOSFET R_ds(on) at 25 °C, Vgs = 10 V | Case A: 1.2 mΩ (DFN5×6), Case B: 2.5 mΩ (DFN3.3×3.3, realistic for nano) |
| α | R_ds(on) temperature coefficient | 0.006 /K |
| t_r, t_f | Switching transition times | 20 ns each |
| t_dt | Dead time per edge | 200 ns |
| V_f | Body-diode forward voltage at 80 A | 0.8 V |
| Q_rr | Body-diode reverse-recovery charge | 50 nC |
| Q_g | Total gate charge | 50 nC |
| C_oss | Output capacitance (charge-equivalent) | 1.5 nF |
| V_drv | Gate drive voltage | 10 V |
| R_Cu | Copper path resistance per channel (bus + phase pads) | 0.5 mΩ |

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Temperature-dependent R_ds(on)

$$R_{ds}(T_j) = R_{ds,25}\,[1 + \alpha\,(T_j - 25)]$$

At T_j = 100 °C: factor = 1.45.
- Case A: 1.2 mΩ → **1.74 mΩ**
- Case B: 2.5 mΩ → **3.63 mΩ**

### 1.2 Current path in 6-step trapezoidal commutation

At any instant, two phases are active:
- **PWM leg:** current flows through either the high-side FET (on-time, duty D) or the synchronous-rectifying low-side FET (off-time, 1 − D), minus dead time.
- **Return leg:** current flows through a static low-side FET.

So two R_ds(on) are always in series:

$$P_{cond,ch} = I_{pk}^2 \cdot 2R_{ds}(T_j)$$

This assumes flat-top current. Ripple adds a factor of $1 + \frac{1}{12}(\Delta I/I)^2$, which is negligible at 48 kHz with typical motor inductance (~10–30 µH).

**Case A:**
P = 80² × 2 × 1.74 mΩ = **22.3 W per channel**

**Case B:**
P = 80² × 2 × 3.63 mΩ = **46.5 W per channel**

### 1.3 Copper loss

$$P_{Cu} = I_{pk}^2 R_{Cu} = 6400 \times 0.5\,\text{m}\Omega = \mathbf{3.2\ W/channel}$$

With 2 oz outer and 2 oz inner copper, 0.5 mΩ is optimistic for a nano layout. Measure it with a 4-wire milliohm meter on first articles.

### 1.4 Electro-thermal fixed point

R_ds depends on T_j, which in turn depends on losses. Iterate:

$$T_j^{(n+1)} = T_{ref} + R_{\theta,eff}\cdot P\!\left(R_{ds}(T_j^{(n)})\right)$$

Thermal runaway occurs when:

$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial T_j}\,R_{\theta,eff} = I^2\cdot 2R_{ds,25}\,\alpha\,R_{\theta,eff} \geq 1$$

For Case A, the runaway threshold is R_θ,eff ≥ 1/(6400 × 2.4 mΩ × 0.006) ≈ **10.9 K/W**. A nano board in prop-wash sits near 5 K/W (Section 3), so it is stable but only ~2× from the threshold. Case B halves that margin.
